clue.text: Dilemma: director in Tesco's fiddled overheads

parts.note: a fix is a tight spot or dilemma

indicators.note: in tells us the director's letter goes inside the store's name
fiddled means tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Tesco is a big British supermarket chain; its name with the S gives the fodder

explanation.surface: A supermarket faces a scandal: a director has been fiddling the books on overheads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' reads as a crooked director's fraud, but it signals the rearrangement, making EDCOSTS; Tesco is a British supermarket chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Overheads are the running costs that stay the same regardless of output, which is exactly what accountants call them.

clue.text: Such blemishes are unusual for a magistrate

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of a magistrate are rearranged, here together with the word are

parts.note: the word are is accounted for in the shuffle: the answer plus these letters make a magistrate

explanation.surface: Marks of this kind would be odd things to find on a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer's letters plus ARE rearrange to make A MAGISTRATE, signalled by 'unusual'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks or blemishes on the body, including the wounds said to mirror Christ's crucifixion.

clue.text: Cargo avoiding Spain for a start

indicators.note: avoiding means doing without, so the letter for Spain is dropped

parts.note: freight is goods carried as cargo
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A ship's load gives Spain a miss, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' reads as 'initially', but 'start' is the definition: a sudden fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden shock or jolt of alarm, the same as a scare.

clue.text: One of 16 useless people

definitions.meaning: 16 across begins with stage; the ... Stage was a famous stagecoach, celebrated in the song from Calamity Jane
unproductive members of a group who contribute nothing

explanation.surface: Someone among the theatre's staff is a waste of space.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference uses the first word of 16 across, STAGE: the Deadwood stage was the coach from the Wild West town.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadwood is idiomatic for people who are no longer useful; Deadwood was also a Wild West town served by its stagecoach.

clue.text: Low needs winds and time to cross Atlantic

indicators.note: the other letters go across, i.e. either side of, the ocean word
winds, as a verb, means twists about, so the letters of needs are rearranged

parts.note: the pond is a jokey name for the Atlantic Ocean

explanation.surface: A sailor waits for the right winds and enough time to make an ocean crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' rearranges NEEDS into DESEN; with T it straddles POND, giving DES-POND-ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low means being dejected or downcast, the mood of someone in despair.

clue.text: Begin to take drugs regularly for that dreamy feeling

indicators.note: to take means to hold within, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: to begin is to start

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of drugs is used

explanation.surface: Someone starts a drug habit to chase a dreamy high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of drugs, D, U and S, which 'take' sits inside START.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a romantic, magical quality or feeling, as in having stardust in one's eyes.

clue.text: A short distance to river wall

parts.note: A, as in one, is the Roman numeral I
mm, a millimetre, is a tiny distance
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: It's only a little way from here to the river wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wall' is a verb here: to wall up.
explanation.definitionFit: To immure someone is to shut them up behind walls, enclosing or imprisoning them.

clue.text: See 4
Bury's outstanding player shouted "Referee!"

parts.note: to bury is to inter; the 's stands for is, joining the pieces

indicators.note: shouted signals that a word is to be taken as spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: A star player from the football club Bury yells at the referee.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is an English football town, so the surface is about a match; 'Referee' is the definition as a verb, to step in between.
explanation.definitionFit: To referee a dispute is to mediate or step in between the parties, as intercession does.

clue.text: Tennyson's first crude poem kept by maestro

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the poet's name is used
crude means rough and unrefined, so the letters of poem are rearranged

explanation.surface: A conductor keeps hold of Tennyson's first rough verse draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by maestro' looks like a container instruction, but it is the definition: a conductor keeps time.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor sets and maintains the speed of the music, which is what musicians call its pace.

clue.text: Took on old English, swapping parts

indicators.note: swapping parts tells us the two pieces come in the opposite order to the clue's

parts.note: aged means old

explanation.surface: Someone took on Old English and found its parts changed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping parts' means the two pieces appear in the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone is to hire them, so engaged means took on as staff.

clue.text: See 22 down
Court service admitted trickery

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the service goes inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A court case where a public body confessed to deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft can mean cunning or guile, skill used to deceive.

clue.text: Plug new gold bed till thoroughly sick of it

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, an ad
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a seam is a bed or layer of coal or ore

explanation.surface: An advert for a new golden bed is repeated till everyone is fed up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means to the point of nausea, i.e. repeated until utterly tiresome.

clue.text: One line transformed into a complex Brechtian effect

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the letters of line and into a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A single line of a play is turned into an elaborate Brechtian device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One line' looks like a single unit of fodder, but 'One' stands apart as A; 'transformed' makes LIENATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt, rendered in English as the alienation effect, keeps audiences emotionally distanced from a play.

clue.text: When queens made out in disguise?

indicators.note: made out is read as made spread out, opening to hold the other pieces

parts.note: as means when
Qu is an abbreviation for queen
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen

explanation.surface: Queens in disguise, playing at being someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queens' is plural, so it supplies two different abbreviations for a queen; 'out' has the outer word opened up to hold the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a pretence or false show, a form of disguise.

clue.text: Men Only issues cover playing field, 22 down's one of them

parts.note: a stag party is for men only

indicators.note: cover means go round, so the issues word wraps the playing field

parts.note: editions are issues of a publication
a rec, short for recreation ground, is a playing field

explanation.surface: A men's magazine's issues report on a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: Men Only is also a British men's magazine title, so 'issues' seems to follow on naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous instruction in The Winter's Tale at 22 down is a printed note telling actors what to do.

clue.text: Cast of ten performed this in Paris foyer

indicators.note: a cast of something is a fresh shaping of it, so the letters of ten are rearranged

parts.note: ran means operated or performed
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A cast of ten put on this show in a Paris theatre lobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the hall or lobby where one comes in, a way in to a building.

clue.text: Old big-chested guys' backstreet scraps

parts.note: DD is a large bra cup size
guys are men
read as back street: ST, the abbreviation for street, written backwards

explanation.surface: Old, busty blokes squabble in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstreet' splits into back + street: ST turned round gives TS.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover bits and pieces, the remnants after the main use.

clue.text: Insurance for theatrical feats spanning river?

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the rearranged letters go either side of the river
theatrical means staged for show, so the letters of feats are rearranged

parts.note: the Tyne is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Acrobats performing feats over a river would want some insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatrical' rearranges the fodder into SAFET, which 'spanning' wraps round the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A safety net is a fallback protection against loss or failure, like an insurance policy.

clue.text: Federer starts serving well opposite

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: acing means serving an unreturnable ace in tennis

explanation.surface: Roger Federer begins a match serving well against his rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Facing means directly across from, so the house facing the park is opposite it.

clue.text: Sage in 5 Hindu borders

parts.note: 5 down means low, dejected, which is sad

indicators.note: borders means the edges, so only the first and last letters of Hindu are used

explanation.surface: A wise man sits within the borders of a Hindu land.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man or wise ascetic, the sort of figure called a sage.

clue.text: High-spirited doctor, one who 25 in hospital?

indicators.note: in means the actor goes inside the hospital word

parts.note: san, short for sanatorium, is a hospital
25 across means overacted; one who overacts is a ham

explanation.surface: An overexcited medic who plays to the gallery in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-spirited' is not lively: it means dealing with high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a healer who works through contact with the spirit world, a witch doctor.

clue.text: Bent front off charm

indicators.note: front off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a bent is a liking or penchant

explanation.surface: A bent front panel spoils an ornament's charm.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm is to delight or bewitch, the same as to captivate.

clue.text: Lacking love, baby due to expire, Ursa involved — best known of 16?

indicators.note: lacking means doing without, so the letter for love is not part of the result
involved means tangled up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Without love, a baby is about to die, with the Great Bear somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: BABY DUE TO EXPIRE URSA minus O is rearranged, as 'involved' signals; 'Lacking love' drops the O. Ursa (bear in Latin) is a hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Winter's Tale has the most famous stage instruction ever written, Antigonus leaving pursued by an animal.

clue.text: See 22 down
Last platform that's retained by its former operating company

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so the abbreviation goes within the company's letters

parts.note: BR, British Rail, formerly ran the platforms of Britain's railways
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A railway's last platform is held by its old operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last platform' is the definition: the stand for a coffin, one's final resting place before burial.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is the stand on which a coffin rests, the final platform anyone lies on.

clue.text: Radio Nicosia's dialect?

indicators.note: Radio Nicosia's reads as Radio Nicosia has, so the letters are contained in these words

explanation.surface: What language does a Cypriot radio station broadcast in?
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic was one of the ancient Greek dialects, spoken in Ionia and the Aegean islands.

clue.text: Was very camp redcoat sacked about a quarter past five?

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other two
sacked means ransacked, so the letters of redcoat are rearranged
past means after, putting the quarter after the five

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
E, east, is one of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: A holiday-camp entertainer, a redcoat, was fired at quarter past five for being too camp.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcoats are entertainers at British holiday camps. 'sacked' turns REDCOAT into ORACTED, round VE.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp means exaggerated and theatrical, so being very camp is acting in an exaggerated way.
